AI-ConneX

IN-HOUSE AGENT METAPHOR SYSTEM

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-017-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX InHouse Metaphorical Agents Catalogue and Architecture | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: Architecture | Section: 1. Executive Summary | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: PreUploadAgent, ScoutAgent, WorkflowPlanner, JudgeAgent, SelectorAgent, ScorerAgent]

AI-ConneX uses many internal agents. Naming every internal agent only by an engineering function can make the architecture difficult for industrial users to understand. The proposed Metaphorical Agent layer gives each agent a controlled, domain-appropriate metaphor: a familiar role or object that explains its responsibility without pretending that the software is human.

The metaphor is a user-interface and communication device, not an implementation dependency. Internal IDs remain stable technical identifiers; the metaphor is a presentation label stored in a governed registry. This distinction is essential for industrial safety, auditability and localization.

Research supports the idea that metaphors can improve comprehension of unfamiliar interfaces, but also shows that metaphor choice changes perceptions of AI competence, warmth and willingness to collaborate. Therefore AI-ConneX must select metaphors systematically, validate them with target users, and explicitly disclose the underlying technical capability and limitations. citeturn0search2turn0search1

For manufacturing specifically, research on industrial icons and visual analytics indicates that semantic alignment between a visual representation and its underlying industrial entity can improve search efficiency and cognitive performance. citeturn0search12turn0search7

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-017-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX InHouse Metaphorical Agents Catalogue and Architecture | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: Architecture | Section: 2. What a Metaphorical Agent Is | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: PreUploadAgent, ScoutAgent, WorkflowPlanner, JudgeAgent, SelectorAgent, ScorerAgent]

Example: the technical agent `dataset_join_validator` may be presented as the **Bridge Inspector** because it checks whether two data structures can be safely connected. The agent does not literally inspect a physical bridge and must not claim physical authority.

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Technical Agent | Executable software component with a defined input, output, policy and tool scope. |
| Metaphorical Agent | The user-facing conceptual role assigned to a technical agent to make its responsibility understandable. |
| Metaphor | A familiar source concept used to explain a less familiar technical responsibility. |
| Metaphor Label | Short name displayed in Jane, logs, stage explanations or visualizations. |
| Metaphor Contract | Governed mapping: technical agent → metaphor → scope → allowed claims → UI language. |
| Metaphor Selector | Internal service that chooses a validated metaphor based on agent role, studio, process and user context. |
| Metaphor Validator | Tests semantic fit, ambiguity, anthropomorphism, safety and comprehension. |

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-017-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX InHouse Metaphorical Agents Catalogue and Architecture | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: Architecture | Section: 3. Design Principles | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: PreUploadAgent, ScoutAgent, WorkflowPlanner, JudgeAgent, SelectorAgent, ScorerAgent]

Metaphors must explain, never conceal.

One technical responsibility should have one primary metaphor per user context.

Metaphors must be familiar to the target industrial audience.

Prefer industrial/process/object metaphors over exaggerated human personas.

Do not imply human consciousness, emotions, legal authority or independent accountability.

Do not imply physical safety certification unless the agent actually performs a certified function.

Metaphor labels are versioned and governed like product terminology.

Every metaphor has a plain-language explanation available on hover/click.

Metaphors must be consistent across Studios.

Safety-critical actions use explicit technical action labels in addition to metaphors.

Metaphor changes must not change agent behavior.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-017-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX InHouse Metaphorical Agents Catalogue and Architecture | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: Architecture | Section: 4.1 Conceptual Metaphor Research | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: PreUploadAgent, ScoutAgent, WorkflowPlanner, JudgeAgent, SelectorAgent, ScorerAgent]

Interface-metaphor research describes metaphor as presenting a new idea in terms of a familiar one and proposes systematic steps for selecting, implementing and evaluating interface metaphors. It also warns that recognition of the metaphor and its relationship to actual functionality are critical. citeturn0search2

Research on conceptual metaphors in human-AI collaboration found that metaphor framing can influence perceived warmth, competence, usability and willingness to cooperate even when the underlying agent behavior is unchanged. This is a direct reason AI-ConneX needs governance rather than ad-hoc naming. citeturn0search1turn0search4

Research on visual metaphors found that schema congruency and contextual detail can improve comprehension of complex data interfaces. citeturn0search5

Recent work on industrial icons reports that metaphorical object representations can affect cognitive performance, while studies of industrial process icons emphasize semantic-entity relevance and search efficiency. citeturn0search7turn0search12

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-017-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX InHouse Metaphorical Agents Catalogue and Architecture | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: Architecture | Section: 4.2 Manufacturing Visualization Basis | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: PreUploadAgent, ScoutAgent, WorkflowPlanner, JudgeAgent, SelectorAgent, ScorerAgent]

NIST describes visual analytics as analytical reasoning facilitated by interactive visual interfaces and identifies benefits for manufacturing including operational decision-making, communication across engineering teams, knowledge transfer and support for less experienced users. citeturn0search6

NIST's machine-maintenance research demonstrates coordinated visual analytics for heterogeneous maintenance data and emphasizes human-in-the-loop interpretation. citeturn0search3

These findings support AI-ConneX using metaphors as a thin comprehension layer over evidence-rich visualizations, rather than using metaphors as substitutes for evidence.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-017-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX InHouse Metaphorical Agents Catalogue and Architecture | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: Architecture | Section: 10. The Metaphor Selector | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: PreUploadAgent, ScoutAgent, WorkflowPlanner, JudgeAgent, SelectorAgent, ScorerAgent]

AI-ConneX should not ask an LLM to invent a metaphor at runtime and immediately display it. Instead, a governed Metaphor Registry stores approved metaphors. A selector ranks approved candidates and a validator rejects poor matches.

Agent Role   ↓Studio + Process Context   ↓Metaphor Registry   ↓Candidate Ranking   ↓Semantic / Safety Validation   ↓User-context suitability   ↓Approved Metaphor   ↓Jane + UI + Documentation

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-017-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX InHouse Metaphorical Agents Catalogue and Architecture | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: Architecture | Section: 12. Metaphor Failure Modes | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: PreUploadAgent, ScoutAgent, WorkflowPlanner, JudgeAgent, SelectorAgent, ScorerAgent]



| Failure | Example | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Over-humanization | 'Expert Engineer' implies human expertise | Users over-trust agent | Prefer Inspector/Lens/Planner |
| Over-competence | 'Master' suggests near-perfect ability | Unsafe reliance | Use bounded functional role |
| Wrong domain | 'Doctor' for data quality | Confusing analogy | Use industrial quality metaphor |
| Mixed metaphor | Bridge + factory + courtroom language in one flow | Cognitive load | One metaphor family per stage |
| Literal confusion | 'Gatekeeper' interpreted as access security when it is only validation | Wrong expectation | Show plain-language definition |
| Safety implication | 'Safety Inspector' without certified safety role | Potential hazard | Reserve safety terms for actual validated safety functions |
| Anthropomorphic accountability | 'The agent decided' | Responsibility confusion | Say 'the system recommended' |
| Cultural mismatch | Metaphor unfamiliar in target plant | Low comprehension | Local user validation |
| Translation drift | Metaphor loses meaning in another language | Misunderstanding | Locale-specific registry |
| Metaphor fatigue | Every microservice gets a colorful name | Noise | Expose only meaningful user-facing agents |
| Branding over clarity | Cute names replace function | Reduced transparency | Always display technical function on demand |
| Runtime hallucination | LLM invents metaphor | Inconsistent UI | Registry-only selection |

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-017-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX InHouse Metaphorical Agents Catalogue and Architecture | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: Architecture | Section: 13. Key R&D Failures Found | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: PreUploadAgent, ScoutAgent, WorkflowPlanner, JudgeAgent, SelectorAgent, ScorerAgent]

Initial assumption: every internal agent needs a memorable metaphor. Finding: too many metaphors increase cognitive load.

Initial assumption: human job titles are easiest. Finding: they can imply authority, competence and accountability that the software does not possess.

Initial assumption: one metaphor works for every audience. Finding: operator, engineer and executive mental models differ.

Initial assumption: metaphor can be generated freely by an LLM. Finding: terminology drift and unsafe claims can occur.

Initial assumption: metaphors can replace technical explanations. Finding: industrial users still need evidence and exact status.

Initial assumption: visual metaphors are universally understood. Finding: cultural and domain context changes comprehension.

Initial assumption: metaphor is cosmetic. Finding: research shows metaphor changes perceptions of AI competence and cooperation.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-017-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX InHouse Metaphorical Agents Catalogue and Architecture | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: Architecture | Section: 14. How AI-ConneX Overcomes These Failures | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: PreUploadAgent, ScoutAgent, WorkflowPlanner, JudgeAgent, SelectorAgent, ScorerAgent]



| Problem | AI-ConneX control |
| --- | --- |
| Too many metaphors | Only user-relevant agents receive metaphors in default UI. |
| Anthropomorphism | Industrial object/process vocabulary is preferred. |
| Overtrust | Metaphor always paired with capability and limitation text. |
| Inconsistent names | Central registry + version control. |
| LLM hallucinated labels | LLM may recommend; registry decides. |
| Cross-Studio inconsistency | Shared metaphor ontology. |
| Safety confusion | Restricted vocabulary for safety-critical terms. |
| Localization | Locale-aware metaphor registry. |
| Changing behavior | Metaphor is presentation metadata, not executable logic. |
| Audit needs | Metaphor ID/version is recorded with UI/event snapshots. |

section: 16. Input from Previous Stage — Jane / Chatbot
text:
[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-017-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX InHouse Metaphorical Agents Catalogue and Architecture | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: Architecture | Section: 16. Input from Previous Stage — Jane / Chatbot | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: PreUploadAgent, ScoutAgent, WorkflowPlanner, JudgeAgent, SelectorAgent, ScorerAgent]

Jane is the human-facing predecessor to the internal agent layer. Jane's output should be normalized into an Intent Envelope. Internal agents consume the envelope rather than parsing raw conversation independently.

{  "intent_uid": "INT-...",  "tenant_uid": "TEN-...",  "user_uid": "USR-...",  "studio": "DATA|ML|AGENTIC",  "goal": "...",  "constraints": ["..."],  "data_refs": ["..."],  "desired_outputs": ["..."],  "risk_class": "normal|high|critical",  "user_role": "...",  "conversation_summary": "...",  "language": "en-IN"}

The Metaphor layer uses the intent envelope only to choose the appropriate vocabulary/context. It must not change the user's technical intent.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-017-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX InHouse Metaphorical Agents Catalogue and Architecture | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: Architecture | Section: 26. Jane Integration | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: PreUploadAgent, ScoutAgent, WorkflowPlanner, JudgeAgent, SelectorAgent, ScorerAgent]

Jane should introduce a metaphor only when it helps comprehension. The recommended response pattern is: metaphor first, technical identity second, evidence third.

"Think of the Profiler as a Surveyor.It measures the shape and quality of your dataset.Technical stage: Data Profiler.Current status: Ready.Evidence: 84 columns profiled; 3 quality warnings."

This prevents the metaphor from becoming a substitute for technical truth.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-017-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX InHouse Metaphorical Agents Catalogue and Architecture | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: Architecture | Section: 28. Metaphor Evaluation POC | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: PreUploadAgent, ScoutAgent, WorkflowPlanner, JudgeAgent, SelectorAgent, ScorerAgent]

POC objective: determine whether metaphor labels improve task comprehension without increasing unsafe overtrust.

Recruit representative plant engineers, maintenance personnel, plant managers and data/ML specialists.

Give participants the same AI-ConneX workflow with and without metaphors.

Measure time to identify what each agent does.

Measure error rate when predicting what an agent can and cannot do.

Measure ability to locate evidence and stage status.

Measure perceived competence and trust.

Test high-risk labels such as Gatekeeper, Inspector, Operator and Sentinel.

Test localized versions if required.

Collect confusion points and revise registry.

Freeze only metaphors that pass comprehension and safety thresholds.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-017-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX InHouse Metaphorical Agents Catalogue and Architecture | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: Architecture | Section: 32. Security and Safety Considerations | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: PreUploadAgent, ScoutAgent, WorkflowPlanner, JudgeAgent, SelectorAgent, ScorerAgent]

Do not allow a metaphor to grant or imply permissions.

Do not expose hidden tenant information through metaphor selection.

Do not include sensitive plant names, asset IDs or secrets in metaphor metadata.

Keep LLM-generated candidate suggestions separate from approved production vocabulary.

Record who approved a metaphor and when.

Use technical labels in machine-to-machine APIs.

Require explicit confirmation for action-producing agents.

Treat 'Operator', 'Controller', 'Safety Inspector' and similar terms as controlled vocabulary.

Keep a fallback technical label if metaphor service is unavailable.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-017-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX InHouse Metaphorical Agents Catalogue and Architecture | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: Architecture | Section: 36. Final Architecture Decision | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: PreUploadAgent, ScoutAgent, WorkflowPlanner, JudgeAgent, SelectorAgent, ScorerAgent]

AI-ConneX should implement a **Metaphorical Agent Registry and Selector as a governed presentation service**, not as a free-form LLM naming feature. The technical agent remains the source of truth. The metaphor is a controlled mental-model aid.

The ideal user experience is:

Jane:"Your Surveyor has finished profiling the data."Technical:Data Profiler — READYEvidence:84 columns • 1.2M rows • 93% quality score • 3 warningsNext:DAG / Family assignment is now available.

This pattern gives industrialists the familiarity of a real-world workflow while preserving the precision, evidence and accountability required by an industrial AI platform.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-017-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX InHouse Metaphorical Agents Catalogue and Architecture | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: Architecture | Section: 37. Conclusion | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: PreUploadAgent, ScoutAgent, WorkflowPlanner, JudgeAgent, SelectorAgent, ScorerAgent]

The Metaphorical Agent layer can become an important part of AI-ConneX's human-centered architecture, provided it remains subordinate to technical truth. The strongest design is not to turn software into fictional employees. It is to give complex technical functions familiar industrial mental models: Adapter, Surveyor, Inspector, Route Map, Workshop, Test Bench, Blueprint, Control Room, Lens and Logbook.

This approach is particularly suitable for AI-ConneX because the platform already uses progressive visualization and Jane as the conversational interface. Metaphors become the connective vocabulary between Jane, stage tabs, visual evidence and internal agents—making a sophisticated multi-agent industrial system easier to learn, navigate and audit.
